study: The 75 cm build's budget, rebuilt with designlab/cost.py (JETSON_PLEM_REVIEW.md section 5, task 9)
status: planning estimate; nothing is built, quoted, measured or adopted

kinds.c: a sourced fact: a catalog price in designlab/data, named by its id
kinds.d: an estimate: the cost model (designlab/cost.py, decision-log A8) or a line estimated here
kinds.c+d: catalog prices (c) with an estimate (d) on top or in them: the cost model's allowance, or an assumed count or choice of part

p4.statement: $10-20 k prototype including outsourced fabrication, integration and spares
p4.why: P4 includes integration and spares, and the cost model's total holds both (the integration line is the subcontract fit-up)

leg_actuators.basis: 12 leg drives at catalog prices; the high case adds 5 %

expression_actuators.basis: neck and tail servos at catalog prices; the high case adds 5 %

compute.basis: the computer's catalog price + $60 / $120 / $200 for storage, fan duct, mounts and leads

rgbd_camera.basis: catalog price + $15 / $35 / $80 for the lead and mount

battery.basis: one pack at catalog price + $30 / $60 / $100 for the cassette

control.basis: PR #662's 60 cm lot, not scaled (Teensy 4.1, two CAN transceivers, IMU; the 60 cm hardware basis also names a TTL servo-bus interface)

power.basis: PR #662's 60 cm lot for a 24 V bus, not scaled

frame.basis: PR #662's 60 cm lot x (structure mass / 1.79 kg)^0.6

covers.basis: PR #662's 60 cm lot x (cover volume / 480 cm3)^0.85

bench.basis: PR #662's 60 cm lot, not scaled (H is not above 0.6 m)

spares.basis: two of the dearest leg drive and one pack at catalog prices + $150 / $350 / $650

class_labels.new_c: new line, catalog price; the count or the part is assumed

frame_6061.how: the record has no structure_material override, and its frame line equals cost.REF['frame'] x its frame_factor with no material factor; the committed 2.54 mm plate lever on 75-M-T-10 (fixed_drives.json, mat75_thinal) costs exactly what its reference does
frame_6061.lot_scope: structure, bearings, hubs, soles, fasteners: scales with structure mass^0.6

covers_pa11.how: the record has no cover_material or cover_wall_scale override, and its cover volume driver equals its cover mass over the default material's density, so its covers line is PA12 at full walls

rule_on_the_recorded_lever.what: the same rule on 75-M-T-10 (targeted_75), against the lever's recorded cost (mat75_pa11)

pad_treads.how: the frame lot of cost.py names soles in its scope, and the record's foot mass (with P20's bigger feet: toe_scale 1.15, pad_scale 1.25) is inside the structure mass that scales that lot; no line names a tread compound or a floor test
pad_treads.lot_scope: structure, bearings, hubs, soles, fasteners: scales with structure mass^0.6

dc_input_and_boom.how: the record has no power_mode override and its battery line is the pack plus the cassette allowance; the bench lot's scope names the tether supply and the catch frame, so the bench supply is not added again; no line names an onboard DC input, a power path or a boom
dc_input_and_boom.not_checked: cost.py gives the power lot no scope, so its contents could not be checked: the 60 cm robot's hardware basis names a regenerative clamp with its regulators, and the DC input line prices a clamp too
dc_input_and_boom.lot_scope: tether supply, charger, cradle/catch frame, instrumentation

compute_allowance.how: cost.py adds $60 / $120 / $200 to the computer's price; build.py's compute tray names what it stands for (NVMe storage, fan duct, mounts, leads), so no separate storage line is added for the Jetson.  The Pi 5 set's catalog price already holds a USB SSD, so the record's compute line counts storage twice and the Jetson's once (compute_difference)

head_record.what: cost.estimate on the expressive head's record against that record's cost block

totals_from_rounded_lines.what: the totals rebuilt from the record's rounded lines against the record's totals

additivity.what: each scenario priced in one call against the baseline plus its blocks priced alone

regulator_12v.label: 6S-to-12 V regulator for the dev kit's carrier (decision-log E7), if it is bought separately
regulator_12v.basis: the prices are the catalog's (c); the choice of part per case is an assumption (d).  Low: the 4.5 A part; nominal and high: the 9 A part (no power mode is chosen, and the larger part covers both modes with room for USB loads).  Both accept the 6S bus; E7 rules the D36V50F12 out only on 12S
regulator_12v.caution: probably already in the power lot, and not a cost of the Jetson alone (section 3.2).  The lot is the 60 cm robot's, whose hardware basis lists a D36V50F12 for its computer (r0_posture_study_2026-11-07/study/hardware/component_basis.md); E7 calls that part the incumbent; the compute survey lists the dev kit's 12 V converter as existing and not counted, and the Pi 5 set's 5 V / 5 A regulator as not priced.  The lot's own breakdown is not in this repository
